text: Water molecules cross this membrane in both directions all the time; in real cells they cross the bilayer and, in many cells, channel proteins too. The sucrose here does not pass. More water molecules cross from the higher water potential, so there is a net movement to the lower side. That is osmosis: the net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential, through a partially permeable membrane. Now add solute to the left until the water potentials are equal. The net arrow fades, but water still crosses both ways.
